claims.text: Introducing a controlled amount of porosity into as-cast HfMoTaTiZr can reduce its density without sacrificing its mechanical properties.
The intervention is the introduction of controlled porosity.
The proposed intervention is applicable from room temperature through 1000 °C.
Porosity is the structural mediator produced by the intervention.
Controlled porosity reduces the overall density of HfMoTaTiZr.
Introducing controlled porosity preserves the alloy's microstructure and composition.
Preservation of the microstructure and composition allows strength to be maintained despite the porosity.
The predicted outcome is lower density without a significant loss of mechanical properties.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has mechanical properties at room and elevated temperature that the intervention is intended to preserve.
The baseline is as-cast HfMoTaTiZr without porosity.
The proposed loading boundary includes both tensile and compressive loading.
The optimal amount of porosity is unknown.
The method for introducing the porosity is unknown and requires investigation.
Samples with multiple porosity levels should be manufactured and mechanically tested at room and elevated temperatures.
Failure to achieve a significant density reduction without compromising mechanical properties would reject the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says a specific amount of porosity will be introduced, but the uncertainty field states that the optimal amount is unknown, and no amount is actually specified.
